newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Defiant Peters offers no apology to NZ parliament.
newsitem.headline: Defiant Peters offers no apology to NZ parliament.

text.p: A defiant New Zealand Deputy Prime Minister and Treasurer Winston Peters declined an invitation to apologise to parliament on Thursday over a long-running inquiry into an alleged assault by him.
Peters said the parliamentary privileges committee had been incorrect to declare him to have committed an assault, even though it found him not guilty of contempt, as he had not had a fair hearing.
"Had there been a charge formulated and I got a fair hearing on that, and if then I was found guilty, I would apologise. I was not, and therefore I will not," he told a packed house.
Peters has already apologised to John Banks, a backbench National Party MP, who was his victim during a late-night fracas after a debate in the house on March 5.
Banks told the debate that while Peters no longer had to apologise to him personally, he was disappointed by Peters' turning down the request for a wider apology to the house.

"I am sorry Mr Peters that you haven't seen fit to come down to this house and apologise. ... But the select committee said you had an apology (to make) to this house, to the integrity of this house, and what this parliament stands for -- that is freedom of speech in a democracy".

The committee on Wednesday ruled there was not sufficient evidence to find Peters in contempt over the incident, but said he had assaulted Banks and suggested he apologise to the House for what it called "unbecoming" and "unacceptable" behaviour.
In a hard-hitting speech that reflected Peters' training as a lawyer, the New Zealand First leader challenged parliament's grounds for declaring him to have committed an assault at all.
"Was I charged with assault? No," he said.

"I will never be part of this dangerous precedent whereby some unformed charge is heard by a committee and the member is never given a chance to defend himself on that charge and then he's expected to apologise," Peters said.
